text: So rid yourselves of all malice and all deceit, of hypocrisy, envy, and slander of every kind.
Like newborn infants, crave the pure milk of the word, so that by it you may grow up into salvation—
now that you have tasted that the Lord is good.
As you come to him, the living stone—rejected by people but chosen and precious in God's sight—
you yourselves, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
For it stands in Scripture: "See, I lay in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone, and whoever believes in him will never be put to shame."
So this honor belongs to you who believe. But for those who do not believe, "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,"

versions.text: To you who believe, then, he is precious. But for those who do not believe, "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,"
versions.explanation: ἡ τιμή is a noun ("the honor/value") without a stated subject; rendering it "he is precious" supplies a subject and blurs the contrast with the rejecters. Rendering it as honor belonging to believers keeps the Greek structure and the flow into the quotation.

text: and, "A stone that makes them stumble and a rock that trips them up." They stumble because they disobey the word—and to this they were appointed.
But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people belonging to God, so that you may proclaim the mighty acts of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.

versions.text: But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people belonging to God, so that you may proclaim the excellencies of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
versions.explanation: "Excellencies" is an archaic, abstract word that stumbles in oral reading. ἀρετάς here denotes God's praiseworthy deeds/glorious character; "mighty acts" (or "praises") is both accurate and speaks clearly aloud.

text: Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
Beloved, I urge you as strangers and exiles to abstain from the desires of the flesh, which wage war against the soul.
Live such good lives among the nations that, though they accuse you of doing wrong, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day he visits them.

versions.text: Live such good lives among the nations that, though they accuse you of doing wrong, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day he visits us.
versions.explanation: The Greek has no pronoun "us"; the whole clause concerns the unbelieving neighbors who observe the believers' conduct. "Visits us" wrongly shifts the reference to the believing readers and adds content not in the text.

text: For the Lord's sake submit yourselves to every human authority: whether to the emperor, as the supreme power,
or to governors, who are sent by him to punish those who do wrong and to commend those who do right.
For it is God's will that by doing good you should silence the ignorant talk of foolish people.
Live as free people, but do not use your freedom as a cover-up for evil; live as God's slaves.
Honor everyone. Love the brotherhood of believers. Fear God. Honor the emperor.
Servants, submit yourselves to your masters with all respect, not only to those who are good and considerate, but also to those who are harsh.
For it is commendable if someone bears up under the pain of unjust suffering because they are conscious of God.
For what credit is it if you endure a beating for doing wrong? But if you endure suffering for doing good, this is commendable before God.
To this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, that you should follow in his steps.
"He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth."
When they hurled insults at him, he did not retaliate; when he suffered, he made no threats, but entrusted himself to him who judges justly.
He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, so that we might die to sin and live for righteousness. By his wounds you have been healed.
For you were like sheep going astray, but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
